Here is an analogy to anchor the next step. Think of a lambda as a small, self-contained errand runner you dispatch from your kitchen. If the ingredient it needs is already in the pantry (a global variable), it can walk in and grab it any time — no preparation needed. But if the ingredient is sitting on *your* counter (a local variable in the enclosing function), you have to physically hand it to the errand runner before you send it off, or it will have no idea the ingredient exists.

- `[ready]` — capture **by value** (the lambda gets its own copy at the moment of creation)
- `[&ready]` — capture **by reference** (the lambda holds a reference to the original variable)
